# Data and Process Overview

We compiled a collection of validation datasets across diverse forest conditions for this specific analysis project. These datasets consist of coincident aerial point cloud data (including USGS 3DEP ALS, UAS-lidar, and UAS-SfM) paired with field-measured stem maps or plot inventories where species identities are known.

| Name | State | Forest Type | Point Cloud Data | Field Data |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Penobscot Experimental Forest | Maine | northern mixed conifer | ALS | tree locations |
| Manitou Experimental Forest (N1) | Colorado | ponderosa pine | UAS-SfM | tree locations |
| Manitou Experimental Forest (Big Plot) | Colorado | western mixed conifer | UAS-SfM | tree locations |
| CSFS State Forest State Park | Colorado | lodgepole pine | UAS-lidar | plots |
| BLM Dawson Creek | Colorado | pinyon-juniper | UAS-SfM | tree locations |
| Ute Creek | Colorado | | UAS-SfM | plots |
| WFSI Fort Stewart | Georgia | southern yellow pine forest | UAS-lidar | plots |
| WFSI Elgin AFB | Florida | longleaf pine | UAS-lidar | plots |
| Wabikon Lake Forest Dynamics Plot (ForestGEO) | Wisconsin | northern mixed hardwood | ALS | tree locations |
| UC Santa Cruz Forest Ecology Research Plot (ForestGEO) | California | coastal mixed-evergreen & coast redwood | ALS | tree locations |
| Smithsonian Environmental Research Center (ForestGEO) | Maryland | mixed deciduous hardwood | ALS | tree locations |
| Smithsonian Conservation Biology Institute (ForestGEO) | Virginia | mid-atlantic deciduous | ALS | tree locations |

We're going to use this first study site and associated data to demonstrate the entire analysis process which includes:

* [Reference Field Data](#01_fld_dta): load and attempt to standardize the field reference spatial tree inventory and polygon plot data
* [Point Cloud Data](#02_ptcld_dta): process the raw point cloud data to generate the CHM used for individual tree detection
* [Individual Tree Detection](#03_itd): Use the CHM for individual tree detection. This includes many steps.
  - Utilize multiple window functions for ITD
  - Evaluate detection accuracy with segmentation matching of the predicted crowns with the field reference points
  - Select the best performing window function with the ITD result used for the remaining species method validation
* [Species/Genus Prediction](#04_species): Predict species for the point cloud-generated tree list
* [Tree-level Species/Genus Evaluation](#05_tree_acc): Evaluate the tree-level accuracy of the proposed classification method
* [Site-level Species/Genus Evaluation](06_site_acc): Evaluate the site-level accuracy of the proposed classification method based on proportional distributions

## Eglin Air Force Base (Florida)

### Field Data{#01_fld_dta}

Field data from this study site is from: 

* Andrew Hudak, Seth Bigelow, Nuria Sánchez-López, and Vanessa Niemczyk. 2025. Field measurements of coarse wood, duff, litter, and trees for the Eglin Air Force Base 2023 fuels campaign. Wildland Fire Science Initiative (WFSI) [https://doi.org/10.60594/W4RG6P](https://doi.org/10.60594/W4RG6P)

>Field measurements collected before and after 2023 study fires at Eglin Air Force Base (AFB) to document fuel loads (large diameter fuels, litter depth, duff depth) and trees in a 3-year rough in sandhill longleaf pine, and the effects of study fires on these variables. Fuel loads, which were measured along transects, were co-located with tree observations, which were measured within fixed-radius plots. These field observations were also co-located with three-dimensional fuel and laser scan plots to allow for leveraging of these other data.

>After the study fires in March 2023, trees within 10 m of plot center were identified to functional group (pine, hardwood or species), measured for diameter at breast height with a diameter tape, measured for distance from outer bark to plot center, and measured for azimuth from plot center to tree. Some post-processing was done using lidar scans to distinguish between evergreeen and deciduous hardwoods. Saplings were tallied by ordinal quadrant (up to 5 m from plot center). Tree measurements were not taken in unit L25. In unit G20, plots HH01, HH02, HH03, HH04, HH05 were sampled pre-fire but not post fire. In unit G25, plots HH105, HH95, PP16 were sampled pre-fire but not post fire.

according to *Eglin_2022_Tree_and_Transect_Field_Protocol.pdf*, the post-fire sampling protocol for trees was:

I. Determine if plot radius is 8 or 11.3 meters and record on datasheet
  a. If there are 4 or more trees within an 8-meter radius, then the plot radius is 8-meters.
  b. If there are 0 to 3 trees within an 8-meter radius, then increase the plot radius to 11.3-meters.
II. Sample all trees ≥10 cm DBH within the plot radius and over from plot center 
III. Sample all pine saplings ONLY ≥2.5 to 10 cm DBH by recording:
  a. Radius (4 or 5.6m):
    i. If tree sampling radius was 8-meters, then sapling sampling radius = 4-meters
    ii. If tree sampling radius was 11.3-meters, then sapling sampling radius = 5.6-meters
  b. Quadrant = NE, SE, SW, or NW
  c. Count = How many of the same species in that quadrant
  d. Species = Longleaf pine (Pinus palustris), Loblolly pine (Pinus taeda), Sand pine (Pinus clausa) or TBD

for those interested, pre- and post-burn photographs for each plot were archived here: [https://doi.org/10.60594/W4GW2T](https://doi.org/10.60594/W4GW2T)

```{r}
# https://doi.org/10.60594/W4RG6P
wfsi_eglinafb_trees <-
  readr::read_csv(
    "../data/WFSI_EglinAFB/Eglin_Air_Force_Base_2023_fuels/data/trees.csv"
    , progress = F
    , show_col_types = F
  ) %>% 
  dplyr::rename_with(~tolower(.x) %>% make.names()) %>% 
  # dplyr::count(species)
  dplyr::filter(
    species != ""
    , !is.na(species)
    , !is.na(tree_x)
    , !is.na(tree_y)
  ) %>% 
  # spatial that
  # epsg from "data_dictionary.csv"
  sf::st_as_sf(coords = c("tree_x", "tree_y"), crs = 26916, remove = F) %>% 
  # make a plot_id that is unique for all so we don't have to join by multiple columns
  # and for all sites we'll just use a plot_id
  dplyr::mutate(
    plot_id = stringr::str_c(unit,plot,sep = "_")
    # also, each tree needs a treeID
    , treeID = dplyr::row_number() %>% as.character()
    # also, we need a species_symbol to match with the FIADatabase
    , species_symbol = toupper(species) %>% stringr::str_remove_all("\\s")
  )
# huh?
wfsi_eglinafb_trees %>% dplyr::glimpse()
# wfsi_eglinafb_trees %>% dplyr::select(dbh_cm) %>% summary()
```

we need to get the plot location points and buffer them by 10 m of plot center which was said to be the field sampling protocol to "*Sample all trees ≥10 cm DBH within the plot radius and over from plot center*" ...clear as mud!

```{r}
# https://doi.org/10.60594/W4T880
wfsi_eglinafb_plots <-
  readr::read_csv(
    "../data/WFSI_EglinAFB/Macroplot_Geographical_Location_Data/data/Geographical_Macroplot_Data_Eglin_2023.csv"
    , progress = F
    , show_col_types = F
  ) %>% 
  dplyr::rename_with(~tolower(.x) %>% make.names()) %>% 
  dplyr::filter(
    !is.na(latitude_y)
    , !is.na(longitude_x)
    , !is.na(macroplot)
  ) %>% 
  # spatial that
  sf::st_as_sf(coords = c("longitude_x", "latitude_y"), crs = 4326, remove = F) %>% 
  # converts proj to match trees and horizontal units to m
  sf::st_transform(sf::st_crs(wfsi_eglinafb_trees)) %>% 
  # "After the study fires in March 2023, trees within 10 m of plot center were identified..."
  sf::st_buffer(10) %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(
    plot_area_m2 = sf::st_area(.) %>% as.numeric()
    # this is good data mgmt: make sure to specify unit orientation in the plot data but not the tree data
    , burn_unit = burn_unit %>% stringr::str_remove("[EWSNewsn]$")
    # # another good practice is to format the plot id's to have padding of two zeros in the plot data but only padding of one zero in the tree data
    , macroplot = dplyr::case_when(
      stringr::str_sub(macroplot, 3, 4) == "00" ~ stringr::str_c( stringr::str_sub(macroplot,1,2), "0", stringr::str_sub(macroplot,5) )
      , stringr::str_sub(macroplot, 3, 3) == "0" ~  stringr::str_c( stringr::str_sub(macroplot,1,2), stringr::str_sub(macroplot,4) )
      , T ~ macroplot
    )
  ) %>% 
  dplyr::rename(
    plot = macroplot
    , unit = burn_unit
  )

# wfsi_eglinafb_plots %>% dplyr::glimpse()
# wfsi_eglinafb_plots$plot %>% unique()
```

```{r}
p_fn_temp <- function(nr){
    p <- wfsi_eglinafb_plots %>% dplyr::slice(nr)

    ggplot2::ggplot() +

      , fill = NA

    ) + 
    ggplot2::geom_sf(
      data = t
      , mapping = ggplot2::aes(color = dbh_cm)
      , size = 2.5
    ) + 
    ggplot2::scale_color_viridis_c(

      , name = "DBH (cm)"

    ggplot2::labs(
      subtitle = paste0(p$unit, " | ", p$plot)
    ) +
    ggplot2::theme_void() +
    ggplot2::theme(
      plot.subtitle = ggplot2::element_text(size = 8, hjust = 0.5, face = "bold")
    )
  }
```

spot check of alignment between plot and tree spatial data looks good but we can quickly look at all plots and trees to see if any trees fall outside of the plot boundaries

```{r}
# wfsi_eglinafb_trees %>% dplyr::glimpse()
wfsi_eglinafb_trees <- 
  1:nrow(wfsi_eglinafb_plots) %>% 
  purrr::map(function(nr){
    p <- wfsi_eglinafb_plots %>% dplyr::slice(nr)
    t <- wfsi_eglinafb_trees %>% 
      dplyr::inner_join(
          p %>% 
          dplyr::select(unit,plot) %>%
          sf::st_drop_geometry()
        , by = dplyr::join_by(unit,plot)
      )
    # points outside?
    out <- t %>% sf::st_filter(p, .predicate = sf::st_disjoint)
      
    return(
      t %>% 
        dplyr::left_join(
          out %>% 
            sf::st_drop_geometry() %>% 
            dplyr::select(plot,unit,tree_number) %>% 
            dplyr::mutate(is_out_of_plot = T)
          , by = dplyr::join_by(plot,unit,tree_number)
        ) %>% 
        dplyr::mutate(
          is_out_of_plot = dplyr::coalesce(is_out_of_plot,F)
        )
    )
  }) %>% 
  purrr::list_rbind()
```

### Point Cloud Data{#02_ptcld_dta}

Andrew Hudak, & Benjamin Bright. (2026). *Airborne Lidar Data from the 2023 Department of Defense Wildland Fire Science Initiative Eglin Air Force Base Campaign*. WFSI Data Portal. [doi:10.60594/W4B017](https://doi.org/10.60594/W4B017)

>This dataset contains airborne light detection and ranging (lidar) data across burn units G20, G25, and L25 in Eglin AFB, FL. Kucera International acquired airborne lidar on January 28, 2023 (before prescribed fire), and on April 26, 2023 (after prescribed fire); prescribed fires occurred from March 11 to 19, 2023. Lidar data were acquired to characterize pre- and post-fire vegetation and estimate fire-caused biomass consumption. 

some other relevant notes about the data:

>Kucera International acquired airborne lidar data across burn units G20, G25, and L25 on January 28, 2023 (before prescribed fire), and across burn units G20 and G25 on April 26, 2023 (after prescribed fire); prescribed fires occurred from March 11 to 19, 2023. The lidar sensor, an Optech Galaxy T2000, was mounted on a PA-31 Piper Navajo Chieftain fixed-wing aircraft, which flew at an elevation of 1341 m (4400 ft) above ground level at a speed of about 150 knots, with a planned sidelap of 30%. The Optech Galaxy T2000 scanned with a laser pulse rate of 1600 kHz, a scan rate of 150 Hz, and a scan field of view of 30 degrees, which resulted in swath widths of 716 meters (2350 feet) and an average point density of 15 points per square meter.

>LAZ file horizontal distance units are meters, in the UTM Zone 16N NAD83 (2011) geographic coordinate system (EPSG 6345)

use `cloud2trees` to process the raw point cloud data to generate a CHM for use in tree detection

```{r}
################################################
# input/output data str
################################################
# outdir
c2t_output_dir_temp <- project_data_df %>% 
  dplyr::filter(tolower(data_site_nm)=="wfsi_eglinafb") %>% 
  dplyr::pull(data_dir)
c2t_process_dir_temp <- file.path(c2t_output_dir_temp, "point_cloud_processing_delivery")
# timer file
c2t_tracking_fnm_temp <- file.path(c2t_process_dir_temp, "processed_tracking_data.csv")
# save to tracking df
project_data_df <- project_data_df %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(
    c2t_process_dir = ifelse(data_dir==c2t_output_dir_temp, c2t_process_dir_temp, "")
    , c2t_tracking_fnm = ifelse(data_dir==c2t_output_dir_temp, c2t_tracking_fnm_temp, "")
  )
# project_data_df %>% print(n=nrow(project_data_df))

################################################
# use point cloud point density
# to automatically set CHM and DTM res
# make a fn to do this based on input LAScatalog
################################################

get_ptcld_density_chm_res_fn <- function(las_ctg, rast_res_buffer = 0.01, min_chm_res_m = 0.15, chm_factor_for_dtm = 2) {
  rast_res_buffer <- dplyr::coalesce(as.numeric(rast_res_buffer),0)
  min_chm_res_m <- dplyr::coalesce(as.numeric(min_chm_res_m),0.15)
  chm_factor_for_dtm <- dplyr::coalesce(as.numeric(chm_factor_for_dtm),2)
  
  if(!inherits(las_ctg, "LAScatalog")){stop("must be a `LAScatalog` read with `lidR::readLAScatalog()`")}
  if(
    !( methods::slotNames(las_ctg) %>% stringr::str_equal("data") %>% any() )
  ){stop("can't find `data` layer in `LAScatalog` read with `lidR::readLAScatalog()`")}
  if(!inherits(las_ctg@data, "sf")){stop("non-sf `data` from `LAScatalog` read with `lidR::readLAScatalog()`")}
  
  # some point clouds have tiles with lots of overlap
  # some point clouds have tiles with no overlap
  
  # union over total area will help us identify overlap
  # high overlap >> union will be much smaller than total area (e.g., uoa ratio < 0.66)
  # low overlap >> union will be similar to total area (e.g., uoa ratio > 0.88)
  
  # union area
  las_uoa_temp <- 
  (
    las_ctg@data %>% 
    dplyr::ungroup() %>% 
    sf::st_union() %>% 
    sf::st_area() %>% 
    as.numeric()
  ) /
  # tot area
  (
    las_ctg@data %>% 
    dplyr::ungroup() %>% 
    dplyr::mutate(
      area_m2 = sf::st_area(geometry) %>% as.numeric()
    ) %>% 
    dplyr::summarise(area_m2=sum(area_m2,na.rm=T)) %>% 
    dplyr::pull(area_m2)
  )
  # las_uoa_temp
  # when a lot of overlap, union and calculate density based off union
  if(las_uoa_temp<0.66){
    pts_m2_temp <- 
      sum(las_ctg@data$Number.of.point.records,na.rm=T) /
      ( las_ctg@data$geometry %>% sf::st_union() %>% sf::st_area() %>% as.numeric() )  
  }else{
  # when NOT a lot of overlap, calculate density as-is
    pts_m2_temp <- 
      las_ctg@data %>% 
      dplyr::mutate(
        area_m2 = sf::st_area(geometry) %>% as.numeric()
      ) %>% 
      sf::st_drop_geometry() %>% 
      dplyr::ungroup() %>% 
      dplyr::summarise(
        pts_m2 = sum(Number.of.point.records,na.rm = T)/sum(area_m2,na.rm = T)
      ) %>% 
      dplyr::pull(pts_m2)
  }
  # pts_m2_temp
  # 1/sqrt(pts_m2_temp)
  
  chm_res_m_temp <- max(round(1/sqrt(pts_m2_temp),2) + rast_res_buffer, min_chm_res_m) 
  dtm_res_m_temp <- round(as.numeric(chm_res_m_temp)*chm_factor_for_dtm,2)
  
  return(list(
    pts_m2 = pts_m2_temp
    , chm_res_m = chm_res_m_temp
    , dtm_res_m = dtm_res_m_temp
  ))
}

# get point cloud density and raster resolutions
get_ptcld_density_chm_res_temp <- get_ptcld_density_chm_res_fn(wfsi_eglinafb_las_ctg_temp)
# get_ptcld_density_chm_res_temp

# fnm
chm_fnm_temp <- file.path(c2t_process_dir_temp, paste0("chm_",get_ptcld_density_chm_res_temp$chm_res_m,"m.tif") )
dtm_fnm_temp <- file.path(c2t_process_dir_temp, paste0("dtm_",get_ptcld_density_chm_res_temp$dtm_res_m,"m.tif") )
# save to tracking df
project_data_df <- project_data_df %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(
    las_pts_m2 = ifelse(data_dir==c2t_output_dir_temp, get_ptcld_density_chm_res_temp$pts_m2, as.numeric(NA))
    , chm_res_m = ifelse(data_dir==c2t_output_dir_temp, get_ptcld_density_chm_res_temp$chm_res_m, as.numeric(NA))
    , chm_fnm = ifelse(data_dir==c2t_output_dir_temp, chm_fnm_temp, "")
    , dtm_res_m = ifelse(data_dir==c2t_output_dir_temp, get_ptcld_density_chm_res_temp$dtm_res_m, as.numeric(NA))
    , dtm_fnm = ifelse(data_dir==c2t_output_dir_temp, dtm_fnm_temp, "")
  )
```

we'll set the minimum CHM resolution to 0.25 m to match the `cloud2trees` default. if the automatically-determined CHM resolution based on the point cloud density used in the `cloud2trees::cloud2raster()` was lower than this level, we'll aggregate the raster using `terra::aggregate()` and `terra::resample()` to get the exact target resolution. if the determined CHM resolution was higher than this level due to low point density, we will use the CHM as-is since this is already the finest resolution possible with the point cloud density.

```{r}
min_chm_res <- 0.25
##################################################################
# aggregate to make raster more coarse for tree detection
##################################################################
agg_chm_rast_fn <- function(chm, res, dir) {
  fp <- file.path(dir, paste0("chm_",res,"m.tif"))
  if(terra::res(chm)[1]<res){
    # first, we'll borrow from the `cloud2trees` codebase to get a function to change the resolution of a raster exactly
    ###___________________________________________###
    # adjust the resolution of a raster to be in exactly the target resolution
    ###___________________________________________###
    if(
      !file.exists(fp)
    ){
      agg_chm_rast <- cloud2trees:::adjust_raster_resolution(
        chm
        , target_resolution = res
        , fun = max
        , resample_method = "max"
        , ofile = fp
      )
    }else{
      agg_chm_rast <- terra::rast( fp )
    }
  }else{
    agg_chm_rast <- chm  
  }
  return(agg_chm_rast)
}

```

### Tree Detection{#03_itd}

`cloud2trees` implements a CHM-based individual tree detection method accessible via `cloud2trees::raster2trees()`. this method requires a window function used to set the search radius used to find local maxima in the CHM. These local maxima represent individual tree top points and are subsequently used to delineate individual tree crowns via a marker-controlled watershed segmentation

because the objective of this study is to evaluate a species/genera classification method, we just want the best ITD results we can get based on the field reference data. We are not interested in evaluating tree segmentation here, that has already been done across varied input data and forest types.

let's make a function to test many different window functions, compare the segmentation results to the field reference data, then select the best window function based on tree detection accuracy.

```{r}
# test a bunch of different variable window sizes within `lidR::lmf()` 
# that cover a range of possibilities and function shapes including linear, concave up, and constant
get_ws_fn_list <- function(min_ws = 0.5, max_ws = 6.0, n_linear = 40, n_concave = 30, n_cr = 30, max_ht = 45) {
  
  # empty list
  ws_functions <- list()
  
  ###########################################################################
  # linear functions over a range
  ###########################################################################
  # end points for the line
  linear_targets <- base::seq(from = max_ws, to = max_ws*4*10, length.out = n_linear)
  
  n_linear_pad <- ceiling(n_linear*1.5)
  
  for (i in 1:n_linear_pad) {
    target_height <- linear_targets[i]
    slope <- (max_ws - min_ws) / target_height
    
    # Pad names with a zero (01 to 60) for clean sorting
    func_name <- base::paste0("linear_", base::sprintf("%02d", i))
    
    v_min  <- base::as.numeric(min_ws)
    v_max  <- base::as.numeric(max_ws)
    v_slope <- base::as.numeric(slope)
    
    func_body <- base::substitute(
      dplyr::case_when(
        base::is.na(x) ~ v_min,
        (v_min + v_slope * x) < v_min ~ v_min,
        (v_min + v_slope * x) > v_max ~ v_max,
        TRUE ~ (v_min + v_slope * x)
      ),
      list(v_min = v_min, v_max = v_max, v_slope = v_slope)
    )
    
    ws_functions[[func_name]] <- base::as.function(c(base::alist(x = ), func_body))
  }
  
  # the flat slopes are too close together...let's remove every other one
  # how many to remove
  num_to_remove <- length(ws_functions) - n_linear
  
  # half
  start_idx <- length(ws_functions) - (num_to_remove - 1) * 2
  
  # remove
  remove_idx <- seq(from = start_idx, to = length(ws_functions), by = 2)
  ws_functions <- ws_functions[-remove_idx]
  names(ws_functions) <- base::paste0("linear_", base::sprintf("%02d", c(1:length(ws_functions)) ))
  
  # ws_functions[1]
  # ws_functions[[1]]
  # class(ws_functions[[1]])
  # ws_functions[[1]](1.5)
  # ws_functions[[1]](0)
  # ws_functions[[1]](18)
  # 
  # ws_functions[[40]](1.5)
  # ws_functions[[40]](0)
  # ws_functions[[40]](18)
  
  ###########################################################################
  # concave down functions over a range
  ###########################################################################
  # total potential growth (or distance) between the floor and the ceiling is: 6.0-0.5=5.5
  # the halfway point of growth is exactly half of that distance: 5.5/2=2.75
  # when the curve reaches its exact halfway point, the resulting window size must be the baseline floor plus that half-distance: 0.5+2.75=3.25
  # in `half_sat`, setting the constant of 1.375 means the function will hit its halfway mark of 3.25 when the tree is only 1.375 meters tall
    # max slope = 4 (for ever 1 m growth, ws increases by 4 m)
    # 4 = (6.0-0.5)/c >> 4 = 5.5/c >> c = 5.5/4 >> c = 1.375
  # how far out to look based on maximum plot/tree height? 45 m tree??
  
  for (i in 1:n_concave) {
    c <- 1.375 # ~dbh height
    max_end <- max_ht # biggest tree everrrrr
    half_sat <- c + (i - 1) * ( (max_end-c) / (n_concave-1))
    
    func_name <- base::paste0("concave_down_", base::sprintf("%02d", i))
    
    v_min  <- base::as.numeric(min_ws)
    v_max  <- base::as.numeric(max_ws)
    v_half <- base::as.numeric(half_sat)
    
    func_body <- base::substitute(
      dplyr::case_when(
        base::is.na(x) ~ v_min,
        (v_min + ((v_max - v_min) * x) / (v_half + x)) < v_min ~ v_min,
        (v_min + ((v_max - v_min) * x) / (v_half + x)) > v_max ~ v_max,
        TRUE ~ (v_min + ((v_max - v_min) * x) / (v_half + x))
      ),
      list(v_min = v_min, v_max = v_max, v_half = v_half)
    )
    
    ws_functions[[func_name]] <- base::as.function(c(base::alist(x = ), func_body))
  }
  # ws_functions[length(ws_functions)]
  # ws_functions[length(ws_functions)-1]
  
  ###########################################################################
  # constant functions over a range
  ###########################################################################
  # range
  constant_values <- base::seq(from = min_ws, to = max_ws * 0.95, by = 0.5)
  
  for (i in base::seq_along(constant_values)) {
    const_val <- constant_values[i]
    
    func_name <- base::paste0("constant_", base::sprintf("%02d", i))
    
    v_min <- base::as.numeric(min_ws)
    v_val <- base::as.numeric(const_val)
    
    func_body <- base::substitute(
      dplyr::case_when(
        base::is.na(x) ~ v_min,
        TRUE ~ v_val
      ),
      list(v_min = v_min, v_val = v_val)
    )
    
    ws_functions[[func_name]] <- base::as.function(c(base::alist(x = ), func_body))
  }
  # ws_functions[length(ws_functions)]
  # ws_functions[[length(ws_functions)]](0.1)
  # ws_functions[[length(ws_functions)]](4)
  # ws_functions[[length(ws_functions)]](15)
  # ws_functions[length(ws_functions)-1]
  
  
  # ###########################################################################
  # # two-step linear functions over a range
  # ###########################################################################
  # # how many functions to test
  # n_temp <- 16
  # # max tree height in CHM
  # 
  # # Calculate fractional boundary envelopes based on global constraints
  # xb_min <- max_ht * 0.09   # ~5m height
  # xb_max <- max_ht * 0.66   # ~25m height
  # yb_min <- min_ws + (max_ws - min_ws) * 0.36  # ~2.5m window size
  # yb_max <- min_ws + (max_ws - min_ws) * 0.88  # ~4.5m window size
  # 
  # xb_sequence  <- base::seq(from = xb_min, to = xb_max, length.out = n_temp)
  # yb_sequence  <- base::seq(from = yb_min, to = yb_max, length.out = n_temp)
  # cap_sequence <- base::seq(from = 15.0,   to = 40.0,   length.out = n_temp)
  # 
  # for (i in 1:n_temp) {
  #   x_b <- xb_sequence[i]
  #   y_b <- yb_sequence[i]
  #   
  #   slope1 <- (y_b - min_ws) / x_b
  #   
  #   target_cap_x <- x_b + cap_sequence[i]
  #   slope2 <- (max_ws - y_b) / (target_cap_x - x_b)
  #   
  #   func_name <- base::paste0("twostep_linear_", base::sprintf("%02d", i))
  #   
  #   v_min    <- base::as.numeric(min_ws)
  #   v_max    <- base::as.numeric(max_ws)
  #   v_xb     <- base::as.numeric(x_b)
  #   v_yb     <- base::as.numeric(y_b)
  #   v_slope1 <- base::as.numeric(slope1)
  #   v_slope2 <- base::as.numeric(slope2)
  #   
  #   func_body <- base::substitute(
  #     dplyr::case_when(
  #       base::is.na(x) ~ v_min,
  #       x <= v_xb ~ {
  #         val <- v_min + v_slope1 * x
  #         dplyr::case_when(val < v_min ~ v_min, val > v_max ~ v_max, TRUE ~ val)
  #       },
  #       x > v_xb ~ {
  #         val <- v_yb + v_slope2 * (x - v_xb)
  #         dplyr::case_when(val < v_min ~ v_min, val > v_max ~ v_max, TRUE ~ val)
  #       }
  #     ),
  #     list(v_min = v_min, v_max = v_max, v_xb = v_xb, v_yb = v_yb, v_slope1 = v_slope1, v_slope2 = v_slope2)
  #   )
  #   
  #   ws_functions[[func_name]] <- base::as.function(c(base::alist(x = ), func_body))
  # }
  # 
  # 
  # # ws_functions[length(ws_functions)]
  # # ws_functions[[length(ws_functions)]](0.1)
  # # ws_functions[[length(ws_functions)]](4)
  # # ws_functions[[length(ws_functions)]](15)
  # # ws_functions[length(ws_functions)-1]
  
  
  ###########################################################################
  # chapman richards functions over a range
  ###########################################################################
  # Generate parameters that smoothly spread across your MAX_CANOPY_HEIGHT
  # Beta controls horizontal stretching; Gamma controls the sharpness of the initial lag
  beta_sequence  <- base::seq(from = 0.15, to = 0.02, length.out = n_cr)
  gamma_sequence <- base::seq(from = 1.5,  to = 4.0,  length.out = n_cr)
  
  for (i in 1:n_cr) {
    b_param <- beta_sequence[i]
    g_param <- gamma_sequence[i]
    
    func_name <- base::paste0("chapman_richards_", base::sprintf("%02d", i))
    
    v_min   <- base::as.numeric(min_ws)
    v_max   <- base::as.numeric(max_ws)
    v_beta  <- base::as.numeric(b_param)
    v_gamma <- base::as.numeric(g_param)
    
    # Chapman-Richards equation with case_when boundaries
    func_body <- base::substitute(
      dplyr::case_when(
        base::is.na(x) ~ v_min,
        TRUE ~ {
          # Core Chapman-Richards Sigmoid Formula
          val <- v_min + (v_max - v_min) * (1 - base::exp(-v_beta * x))^v_gamma
          dplyr::case_when(val < v_min ~ v_min, val > v_max ~ v_max, TRUE ~ val)
        }
      ),
      list(v_min = v_min, v_max = v_max, v_beta = v_beta, v_gamma = v_gamma)
    )
    
    ws_functions[[func_name]] <- base::as.function(c(base::alist(x = ), func_body))
  }
  
  return(ws_functions)
}
```

now we need a function to clip the CHM to the plot plus a buffer and run `cloud2trees::raster2trees()` for each window function. the return should be a spatial tree list unique by function.

```{r}
# function to loop over ws function list in raster2trees
ws_testtest_fn <- function(
    chm
    , buffer = 5
    , plot_sf
    , ws_fn_list # a named list of functions ex: cloud2trees::itd_ws_functions()
  ) {
  # min ht for chm so we can test non-na
  min_chm_ht <- 1.37
  # crop chm
  chm_crop <- chm %>% 
    terra::crop(
      plot_sf %>% 
        sf::st_transform(terra::crs(chm)) %>% 
        sf::st_buffer(buffer)
      , mask = T
    ) %>% 
    terra::clamp(lower = min_chm_ht, values = F)
  
  # terra::plot(chm_crop)
  # terra::plot(
  #   plot_sf %>%
  #     sf::st_transform(terra::crs(chm))
  #   , add = T
  #   , border = "cyan"
  #   , col = NA
  # )

  if( !any( terra::global(chm_crop, fun = "anynotNA") ) ){
    return(NULL)
  }
  
  # map over the function list
  ws_tree_list <- 
    names(ws_fn_list) %>%
    purrr::set_names() %>%
    purrr::map(function(nm){
      if (exists("my_temp_dir") && dir.exists(my_temp_dir)) {
        unlink(my_temp_dir, recursive = TRUE, force = TRUE)
      }
      if (exists("my_temp_dir2") && dir.exists(my_temp_dir2)) {
        unlink(my_temp_dir2, recursive = TRUE, force = TRUE)
      }
      warning(paste0("making dir: ",nm,"....",Sys.time()),immediate. = T,call. = F)
      my_temp_dir <- tempfile(pattern = nm)
      dir.create(my_temp_dir, showWarnings = FALSE)
      my_temp_dir2 <- tempfile(pattern = paste0("xx",nm))
      dir.create(my_temp_dir2, showWarnings = FALSE)
      warning(paste0("raster2trees: ",nm,"....",Sys.time()),immediate. = T,call. = F)
      
      safe_raster2trees <- purrr::safely( cloud2trees::raster2trees )
      xxx_raster2trees_ans <- safe_raster2trees(
          chm_rast = chm_crop
          , outfolder = my_temp_dir
          , ws = ws_fn_list[[nm]]
          , min_height = min_chm_ht
          , min_crown_area = 0.5
          , tempdir = my_temp_dir2
        )
      
      if(!is.null(xxx_raster2trees_ans$result)){
        xxx_raster2trees_ans <- xxx_raster2trees_ans$result
        # xxx_raster2trees_ans %>% names()
        return(
          xxx_raster2trees_ans %>% 
            cloud2trees::simplify_multipolygon_crowns()
            # sf::st_drop_geometry() %>% 
            # sf::st_as_sf(coords = c("tree_x", "tree_y"), crs = sf::st_crs(xxx_raster2trees_ans))
        )
      }else{return(NULL)}
    }) %>% 
    purrr::list_rbind(names_to = "ws_fn_nm")
  
  # ws_tree_list %>% dplyr::glimpse()
  # ws_tree_list %>% sf::st_drop_geometry() %>% dplyr::count(ws_fn_nm)
  # ws_tree_list %>% class()
  
  return(ws_tree_list)
}
```

```{r}
      , by = "join_id"
    )
  # wfsi_eglinafb_ws_pred_trees %>% dplyr::glimpse()
  
  # # plot real quick
  # wfsi_eglinafb_ws_pred_trees %>% 
  #   sf::st_drop_geometry() %>% 
  #   dplyr::slice_sample(n = 9999) %>% 
  #   ggplot2::ggplot(mapping = ggplot2::aes(x=tree_height_m,y=dbh_cm)) + 
  #   ggplot2::geom_point() +
  #   ggplot2::geom_point(mapping = ggplot2::aes(y=fia_est_dbh_cm_lower),color="gray") +
  #   ggplot2::geom_point(mapping = ggplot2::aes(y=fia_est_dbh_cm_upper),color="gray")

  # save
  sf::st_write(wfsi_eglinafb_ws_pred_trees, dsn = fnm_temp, quiet = T, append = F)
}else{
  wfsi_eglinafb_ws_pred_trees <- sf::st_read(fnm_temp, quiet = T)
}
```

now we need a function to perform instance matching of the predictions and reference data. to keep things simple, since all the reference field data includes point locations, we'll perform matching based on a spatial distance mathing of these points with the predicted tree top points using a 2 m search radius. if multiple tree points fall within a the search radius, we'll select the tree that is closest in terms of size based on whatever field data is available (height or DBH). One predicted tree will only be matched with one field reference tree and vice-versa.

```{r, include=F, eval=F}
###############################################################
###############################################################
###############################################################
###############################################################
# check df function
###############################################################
###############################################################
###############################################################
###############################################################
validate_df_fn <- function(data, required_cols = c("tree_height_m"), check_numeric = F) {
  # check data
  if(!inherits(data,"sf") && !inherits(data,"sfc")){stop("all input data requires POINT sf data")}
  if(
    !all( sf::st_is(data, c("POINT")) )
  ){
    stop("all input data requires POINT sf data")
  }
  # names
  # uses base::setdiff and base::names
  missing_cols <- setdiff(required_cols, names(data))
  
  if(length(missing_cols) > 0){
    stop("all input data requires columns: ", paste(missing_cols, collapse = ", "))
  }
  
  # numeric
  if(check_numeric){
    non_numeric <- data %>%
      sf::st_drop_geometry() %>% 
      dplyr::select(dplyr::all_of(required_cols)) %>%
      dplyr::summarise(dplyr::across(dplyr::everything(), ~ !is.numeric(.x))) %>%
      tidyr::pivot_longer(dplyr::everything()) %>%
      dplyr::filter(value == TRUE)

    if (nrow(non_numeric) > 0) {
      stop("columns must be numeric: ", paste(non_numeric$name, collapse = ", "))
    }
  }
  
  # is.na() catches both NA and NaN; is.infinite() catches Inf
  invalid_dta <- data %>%
    sf::st_drop_geometry() %>% 
    dplyr::summarise(
      dplyr::across(
        dplyr::all_of(required_cols)
        , ~ sum(is.na(.x) | is.infinite(.x))
      )
    ) %>%
    tidyr::pivot_longer(
      cols = dplyr::everything()
      , names_to = "column"
      , values_to = "count"
    ) %>%
    dplyr::filter(count > 0)

  if (nrow(invalid_dta) > 0) {
    bad_cols <- paste(invalid_dta$column, collapse = ", ")
    stop("invalid values (NA, NaN, or Inf) found in: ", bad_cols)
  }
  return(TRUE)
}
###############################################################
###############################################################
###############################################################
###############################################################
# match function
###############################################################
###############################################################
###############################################################
###############################################################
reference_prediction_match <- function(
  pred_data
  , ref_data
  , max_dist_m
  , max_error_pct
) {
  #######################################################################
  # threshold checks
  #######################################################################
  if(
    any(is.na(max_dist_m)) || 
    any(is.null(max_dist_m)) || 
    !inherits(as.numeric(max_dist_m),"numeric")
  ){
    stop("`max_dist_m` must be numeric and not missing")
  }else{max_dist_m <- as.numeric(max_dist_m)[1]}
  if(
    any(is.na(max_error_pct)) || 
    any(is.null(max_error_pct)) || 
    !inherits(as.numeric(max_error_pct),"numeric")
  ){
    stop("`max_error_pct` must be numeric and not missing")
  }else{max_error_pct <- as.numeric(max_error_pct)[1]}
  #######################################################################
  # data checks
  #######################################################################
  # set up matching col based on what data is available
  if(
    any( stringr::str_equal(names(pred_data),"tree_height_m") ) &&
    any( stringr::str_equal(names(ref_data),"tree_height_m") )
  ){
    pred_data <- pred_data %>% dplyr::mutate(tree_height_m = as.numeric(tree_height_m))
    ref_data <- ref_data %>% dplyr::mutate(tree_height_m = as.numeric(tree_height_m))
  }else if(
    any( stringr::str_equal(names(pred_data),"dbh_cm") ) &&
    any( stringr::str_equal(names(ref_data),"dbh_cm") )
  ){
    pred_data <- pred_data %>% dplyr::mutate(tree_height_m = as.numeric(dbh_cm))
    ref_data <- ref_data %>% dplyr::mutate(tree_height_m = as.numeric(dbh_cm))
  }else{
    stop("both reference and predicted data must have `tree_height_m` or `dbh_cm` column")
  }
  
  if(
    !any( stringr::str_equal(names(pred_data),"treeID") ) ||
    !any( stringr::str_equal(names(ref_data),"treeID") )
  ){
    stop("both reference and predicted data must have `treeID` column")
  }
  
  if(nrow(pred_data)==0 | nrow(ref_data)==0){
    warning("no data so...?????")
    # return(NULL)
    
    if(nrow(pred_data)!=0){
      pred_data <- cloud2trees:::check_spatial_points(pred_data)
      validate_df_fn(data = pred_data, required_cols = c("tree_height_m"), check_numeric = T)
      # sort to start with largest
      pred_data <- pred_data %>% 
        dplyr::arrange(desc(tree_height_m)) %>% 
        dplyr::mutate(pred_match_idx = dplyr::row_number()) %>% 
        # add columns
        dplyr::mutate(
          ref_match_idx = as.numeric(NA)
          , pred_match_height_diff_m= as.numeric(NA)
          , pred_match_dist_m = as.numeric(NA)
          , ref_tree_height_m = as.numeric(NA)
        )
    }else{pred_data <- NULL}
    
    if(nrow(ref_data)!=0){
      ref_data <- cloud2trees:::check_spatial_points(ref_data)
      validate_df_fn(data = ref_data, required_cols = c("tree_height_m"), check_numeric = T)
      # sort to start with largest
      ref_data <- ref_data %>% 
        dplyr::arrange(desc(tree_height_m)) %>% 
        dplyr::mutate(ref_match_idx = dplyr::row_number()) %>% 
        # add columns
        dplyr::mutate(
          pred_match_idx = 0
          , pred_match_height_diff_m = as.numeric(NA)
          , pred_tree_height_m = as.numeric(NA)
          , pred_match_dist_m = as.numeric(NA)
        )
    }else{ref_data <- NULL}
    # return
    return(list(
      ref_data = ref_data
      , pred_data = pred_data
    ))
  }
  pred_data <- cloud2trees:::check_spatial_points(pred_data)
  validate_df_fn(data = pred_data, required_cols = c("tree_height_m"), check_numeric = T)
  ref_data <- cloud2trees:::check_spatial_points(ref_data)
  validate_df_fn(data = ref_data, required_cols = c("tree_height_m"), check_numeric = T)
  
  # proj
  if(!identical(
    sf::st_crs(pred_data, parameters = T)[["epsg"]]
    , sf::st_crs(ref_data, parameters = T)[["epsg"]]
  )){stop("data must have same projection. see `sf::st_crs()`")}
  # sort to start with largest
  pred_data <- pred_data %>% 
    dplyr::arrange(desc(tree_height_m)) %>% 
    dplyr::mutate(pred_match_idx = dplyr::row_number())
  ref_data <- ref_data %>% 
    dplyr::arrange(desc(tree_height_m)) %>% 
    dplyr::mutate(ref_match_idx = dplyr::row_number())
  #######################################################################
  # build a 2D kd-tree
  #######################################################################
    # Use the X and Y coordinates of the predicted to build the tree.
    pred_coords_temp <- 
      pred_data %>% 
      dplyr::mutate(
        X = sf::st_coordinates(.)[,1] %>% as.numeric()
        , Y = sf::st_coordinates(.)[,2] %>% as.numeric()
      ) %>% 
      dplyr::select(X,Y) %>% 
      sf::st_drop_geometry()
    # Use the X and Y coordinates of the reference to build the tree.
    ref_coords_temp <- 
      ref_data %>% 
      dplyr::mutate(
        X = sf::st_coordinates(.)[,1] %>% as.numeric()
        , Y = sf::st_coordinates(.)[,2] %>% as.numeric()
      ) %>% 
      dplyr::select(X,Y) %>% 
      sf::st_drop_geometry()
    
    # perform a fixed-radius search using RANN::nn2
    nn_ans_temp <- RANN::nn2(
      # the point cloud xy data (builds the kd-tree on this)
      data = pred_coords_temp
      # the seed point xy data (number of columns must be the same as data)
      , query = ref_coords_temp
      # maximum number of neighbors to find per query
      , k = min(nrow(pred_coords_temp),nrow(ref_coords_temp))
      # the search radius (rcyl)
      , radius = max_dist_m
      , searchtype = "radius"
    )
    # huh?
    # nn_ans_temp %>% class()
    # nn_ans_temp %>% names()
    # nn_ans_temp$nn.idx %>% nrow()
    # nrow(ref_coords_temp)
    # nn_ans_temp$nn.idx %>% ncol()
    # nrow(pred_coords_temp)
    # nn_ans_temp$nn.dists %>% nrow()
    # nrow(ref_coords_temp)
    # nn_ans_temp$nn.dists %>% ncol()
    # nrow(pred_coords_temp)
    # nn_ans_temp$nn.dists[1:11,] %>% dplyr::as_tibble() %>% dplyr::glimpse()
  #######################################################################  
  # iterate through the kd-tree to make matches
  #######################################################################
    if(nrow(ref_coords_temp)!=nrow(ref_data)){stop("bad kd-tree")}
    # add pred match tracker
    ref_data$pred_match_idx <- 0
    ref_data$pred_match_height_diff_m <- as.numeric(NA)
    ref_data$pred_tree_height_m <- as.numeric(NA)
    ref_data$pred_match_dist_m <- as.numeric(NA)
    for(i in 1:nrow(ref_coords_temp)){
      # get indices of points in the current cylinder (0 means no point found)
      nn_idx_pts <- nn_ans_temp$nn.idx[i, ]
      cyl_pts <- nn_idx_pts[nn_idx_pts > 0] 
      # remove already matched
      cyl_pts <- cyl_pts[!(cyl_pts %in% ref_data$pred_match_idx)] 
      # if available matches
      if(dplyr::coalesce(length(cyl_pts),0) >= 1) {
        # get heights
        # ref_data %>% dplyr::select(field_tree_id, tree_height_m) %>% dplyr::glimpse()
        # ref_data$tree_height_m[i]
        # pred_data$tree_height_m[cyl_pts]
        ht_diffs <- abs(ref_data$tree_height_m[i]-pred_data$tree_height_m[cyl_pts])/ref_data$tree_height_m[i]
        # get the minimum value among elements below the threshold
        min_val <- min(ht_diffs[ht_diffs <= max_error_pct], na.rm = T)
        # if not none within threshold
        if(!is.infinite(min_val)){
          # the index of that value in the original full vector
          cyl_idx <- which(ht_diffs == min_val)[1] # if multiple matches, takes the nearest
          match_idx <- cyl_pts[cyl_idx]
          # distance
          nn_dist_idx <- which(nn_idx_pts == match_idx)
          nn_dist <- nn_ans_temp$nn.dists[i,nn_dist_idx]
          # update match
          ref_data$pred_match_height_diff_m[i] <- min_val
          ref_data$pred_tree_height_m[i] <- pred_data$tree_height_m[match_idx]
          ref_data$pred_match_idx[i] <- match_idx
          ref_data$pred_match_dist_m[i] <- nn_dist
          
        }
      }
    }
  #######################################################################
  # add ref id to pred and return
  #######################################################################
  # pred_data %>% dplyr::glimpse()
  # ref_data %>% dplyr::glimpse()
  pred_data <- pred_data %>% 
    # get rid of columns we'll create
    dplyr::select( -dplyr::any_of(c(
      "hey_xxxxxxxxxx"
      , "pred_match_height_diff_m"
      , "pred_match_dist_m"
      , "ref_tree_height_m"
      , "ref_match_idx"
    ))) %>% 
    dplyr::left_join(
      ref_data %>% 
        sf::st_drop_geometry() %>% 
        dplyr::select(ref_match_idx, pred_match_idx, pred_match_height_diff_m, pred_match_dist_m, tree_height_m) %>% 
        dplyr::rename(ref_tree_height_m=tree_height_m)
      , by = "pred_match_idx"
    )
  return(list(
    ref_data = ref_data
    , pred_data = pred_data
  ))
}
###############################################################
###############################################################
###############################################################
###############################################################
# combine match to classify reference/predictions
###############################################################
###############################################################
###############################################################
###############################################################
ground_truth_prediction_match <- function(
  reference_prediction_match_ans
  , comp_cols = c("tree_height_m")
) {
  # check for missing both missing
  if(
    is.null(reference_prediction_match_ans$ref_data)
    && is.null(reference_prediction_match_ans$pred_data)
  ){
    warning("no data so...?????")
    return(NULL)
  }
  
  # if reference but no predictions...they are all omissions (FN)
  if(is.null(reference_prediction_match_ans$pred_data)){
    return_df <-
      reference_prediction_match_ans$ref_data %>%
      dplyr::filter(pred_match_idx==0 | is.na(pred_match_idx)) %>% 
      dplyr::rename(ref_treeID=treeID) %>% 
      dplyr::mutate(pred_treeID=as.character(NA)) %>% 
      dplyr::select(dplyr::all_of(c(
        "ref_match_idx"
        , "ref_treeID"
        , "pred_match_idx"
        , "pred_treeID"
        , "pred_match_dist_m"
        # , "pred_tree_height_m"
        # , "tree_height_m"
        , comp_cols
      ))) %>% 
      dplyr::rename_with(
        .cols = dplyr::all_of(comp_cols)
        , .fn = ~paste0("ref_", .x, recycle0 = T)
      ) %>% 
      sf::st_set_geometry("ref_geometry") %>% 
      dplyr::mutate(match_grp = "omission")
    # make match_grp factor
    return_df <- return_df %>% 
      dplyr::mutate(
        match_grp = factor(
          match_grp
          , ordered = T
          , levels = c(
            "true positive"
            , "commission"
            , "omission"
          )
        ) %>% forcats::fct_rev()
      )
    return(return_df)
  }
  
  # if predictions but no reference...they are all commissions (FP)
  if(is.null(reference_prediction_match_ans$ref_data)){
    return_df <-
      reference_prediction_match_ans$pred_data %>%
      dplyr::filter(ref_match_idx==0 | is.na(ref_match_idx)) %>% 
      dplyr::rename(pred_treeID=treeID) %>% 
      dplyr::mutate(ref_treeID=as.character(NA)) %>% 
      dplyr::select(dplyr::all_of(c(
        "ref_match_idx"
        , "ref_treeID"
        , "pred_match_idx"
        , "pred_treeID"
        , "pred_match_dist_m"
        # , "pred_tree_height_m"
        # , "tree_height_m"
        , comp_cols
      ))) %>% 
      dplyr::rename_with(
        .cols = dplyr::all_of(comp_cols)
        , .fn = ~paste0("pred_", .x, recycle0 = T)
      ) %>% 
      dplyr::mutate(pred_geometry = sf::st_geometry(.)) %>%
      sf::st_drop_geometry() %>% 
      dplyr::mutate(match_grp = "commission")
    # make match_grp factor
    return_df <- return_df %>% 
      dplyr::mutate(
        match_grp = factor(
          match_grp
          , ordered = T
          , levels = c(
            "true positive"
            , "commission"
            , "omission"
          )
        ) %>% forcats::fct_rev()
      )
    return(return_df)
  }
  
  ############# otherwise: nrow(ref_data)>0 & nrow(pred_data)>0
  ############# otherwise: nrow(ref_data)>0 & nrow(pred_data)>0
  ############# otherwise: nrow(ref_data)>0 & nrow(pred_data)>0
  ############# otherwise: nrow(ref_data)>0 & nrow(pred_data)>0
  ############# otherwise: nrow(ref_data)>0 & nrow(pred_data)>0
  # check for comparison cols
  comp_cols <- 
    comp_cols %>% 
    # remove whitespace
    stringr::str_trim() %>% 
    # keep only those with a value
    stringr::str_subset(".")
  if(inherits(comp_cols, "character") && length(comp_cols) > 0){
    validate_df_fn(data = reference_prediction_match_ans$ref_data, required_cols = comp_cols, check_numeric = T)
    validate_df_fn(data = reference_prediction_match_ans$pred_data, required_cols = comp_cols, check_numeric = T)
  }
  # tp matches
  return_df <-
    reference_prediction_match_ans$ref_data %>%
    dplyr::filter(pred_match_idx!=0 & !is.na(pred_match_idx)) %>% 
    dplyr::select(dplyr::all_of(c(
      "ref_match_idx"
      , "pred_match_idx"
      , "pred_match_dist_m"
      # , "pred_tree_height_m"
      # , "tree_height_m"
      , comp_cols
    ))) %>% 
    dplyr::rename_with(
      .cols = dplyr::all_of(comp_cols)
      , .fn = ~paste0("ref_", .x, recycle0 = T)
    ) %>% 
    sf::st_set_geometry("ref_geometry") %>% 
    # add on pred geom
    dplyr::inner_join(
      reference_prediction_match_ans$pred_data %>% 
        dplyr::select(dplyr::all_of(c(
          "ref_match_idx"
          , comp_cols
        ))) %>% 
        dplyr::rename_with(
          .cols = dplyr::all_of(comp_cols)
          , .fn = ~paste0("pred_", .x, recycle0 = T)
        ) %>% 
        dplyr::mutate(pred_geometry = sf::st_geometry(.)) %>%
        sf::st_drop_geometry()
      , by = "ref_match_idx"
    ) %>% 
    dplyr::mutate(match_grp = "true positive")
  
  # add omissions
  return_df <-
    return_df %>% 
    dplyr::bind_rows(
      reference_prediction_match_ans$ref_data %>%
        dplyr::filter(pred_match_idx==0 | is.na(pred_match_idx)) %>% 
        dplyr::select(dplyr::all_of(c(
          "ref_match_idx"
          , "pred_match_idx"
          , "pred_match_dist_m"
          # , "pred_tree_height_m"
          # , "tree_height_m"
          , comp_cols
        ))) %>% 
        dplyr::rename_with(
          .cols = dplyr::all_of(comp_cols)
          , .fn = ~paste0("ref_", .x, recycle0 = T)
        ) %>% 
        sf::st_set_geometry("ref_geometry") %>% 
        dplyr::mutate(match_grp = "omission")
    )
    
  # add commissions
  return_df <-
    return_df %>% 
    dplyr::bind_rows(
      reference_prediction_match_ans$pred_data %>%
        dplyr::filter(ref_match_idx==0 | is.na(ref_match_idx)) %>% 
        dplyr::select(dplyr::all_of(c(
          "ref_match_idx"
          , "pred_match_idx"
          , "pred_match_dist_m"
          # , "pred_tree_height_m"
          # , "tree_height_m"
          , comp_cols
        ))) %>% 
        dplyr::rename_with(
          .cols = dplyr::all_of(comp_cols)
          , .fn = ~paste0("pred_", .x, recycle0 = T)
        ) %>% 
        dplyr::mutate(pred_geometry = sf::st_geometry(.)) %>%
        sf::st_drop_geometry() %>% 
        dplyr::mutate(match_grp = "commission")
    )
  
  # make match_grp factor
  return_df <- return_df %>% 
    dplyr::mutate(
      match_grp = factor(
        match_grp
        , ordered = T
        , levels = c(
          "true positive"
          , "commission"
          , "omission"
        )
      ) %>% forcats::fct_rev()
    )
  
  
  if(inherits(comp_cols, "character") && length(comp_cols) > 0){
    # add a tiny value (eps) to the denominator for pct_diff_ 
    # calcs to prevent division by zero...where pct_diff_ is used for MAPE summary
    eps <- 1e-5
    return_df <- 
      return_df %>% 
      dplyr::mutate(
        # 'diff_' columns are calculated as the predicted value minus the actual value
        dplyr::across(
          .cols = paste0(
            "ref_"
            , comp_cols # c("tree_height_m", "dbh_cm")
            , recycle0 = T
          )
          , .fns = ~ base::get(stringr::str_replace(dplyr::cur_column(), "^ref_", "pred_")) - .x
          , .names = "diff_{stringr::str_remove(.col, '^ref_')}"
        )
        # 'pct_diff_' columns are calculated as the actual value minus the predicted value divided by the actual value
        , dplyr::across(
          .cols = paste0(
            "ref_"
            , comp_cols # c("tree_height_m", "dbh_cm")
            , recycle0 = T
          )
          # 
          , .fns = ~ (.x-base::get(stringr::str_replace(dplyr::cur_column(), "^ref_", "pred_")))/(.x + eps)
          , .names = "pct_diff_{stringr::str_remove(.col, '^ref_')}"
        )
      ) 
  }
  
  # add treeID
  return_df <- 
    return_df %>% 
    dplyr::left_join(
      reference_prediction_match_ans$pred_data %>%
        sf::st_drop_geometry() %>% 
        dplyr::distinct(pred_match_idx,treeID) %>% 
        dplyr::rename(pred_treeID=treeID)
      , by = "pred_match_idx"
    ) %>% 
    dplyr::left_join(
      reference_prediction_match_ans$ref_data %>%
        sf::st_drop_geometry() %>% 
        dplyr::distinct(ref_match_idx,treeID) %>% 
        dplyr::rename(ref_treeID=treeID)
      , by = "ref_match_idx"
    ) %>% 
    dplyr::relocate(ref_treeID, .after = ref_match_idx) %>% 
    dplyr::relocate(pred_treeID, .after = pred_match_idx)
  
  
  # return
  if(nrow(return_df)==0){
    warning("no records found for ground truth to predition matching")
    return(NULL)
  }else{
    return(return_df)
  }
  
}
```

```{r}
###########################################################################################
###########################################################################################
## this is for matching predicted crowns to reference points
## this is for matching predicted crowns to reference points
## this is for matching predicted crowns to reference points
## this is for matching predicted crowns to reference points
###########################################################################################
###########################################################################################

# instance matching function for points reference and polys predictions
# matches a single set of predictions with a single reference set
instance_match_fn <- function(
  pred_crowns
  , ref_points
){
  # check
  if(
    !any( stringr::str_equal(names(pred_crowns),"treeID") ) ||
    !any( stringr::str_equal(names(ref_points),"treeID") )
  ){
    stop("both reference and predicted data must have `treeID` column")
  }
  
  if(nrow(ref_points)==0){return(NULL)}
  if(nrow(pred_crowns)==0 && nrow(ref_points)>0){
    return(
      ref_points %>% 
        sf::st_drop_geometry() %>% 
        dplyr::mutate(
          ref_match_idx = dplyr::row_number()
          , pred_match_idx = as.numeric(NA)
        ) %>% 
        dplyr::select(dplyr::all_of(c(
          "ref_match_idx"
          , "pred_match_idx"
        ))) %>% 
        dplyr::mutate(
          match_grp = "omission"
          , match_grp = factor(
            match_grp
            , ordered = T
            , levels = c(
              "true positive"
              , "commission"
              , "omission"
            )
          ) %>% forcats::fct_rev()
        )
    )
  }
  
  # set up matching col based on what data is available
  if(
    any( stringr::str_equal(names(pred_crowns),"tree_height_m") ) &&
    any( stringr::str_equal(names(ref_points),"tree_height_m") )
  ){
    pred_crowns <- pred_crowns %>% dplyr::mutate(xxx_match_col = as.numeric(tree_height_m))
    ref_points <- ref_points %>% dplyr::mutate(xxx_match_col = as.numeric(tree_height_m))
  }else if(
    any( stringr::str_equal(names(pred_crowns),"dbh_cm") ) &&
    any( stringr::str_equal(names(ref_points),"dbh_cm") )
  ){
    pred_crowns <- pred_crowns %>% dplyr::mutate(xxx_match_col = as.numeric(dbh_cm))
    ref_points <- ref_points %>% dplyr::mutate(xxx_match_col = as.numeric(dbh_cm))
  }else{
    stop("both reference and predicted data must have `tree_height_m` or `dbh_cm` column")
  }
  # get rid of data without data
  pred_crowns <- pred_crowns %>% dplyr::filter(!is.na(xxx_match_col), xxx_match_col>0) %>% 
    # make an id
    dplyr::mutate(xxx_id = dplyr::row_number())
  ref_points <- ref_points %>% dplyr::filter(!is.na(xxx_match_col), xxx_match_col>0) %>% 
    # make it the same crs
    sf::st_transform(sf::st_crs(pred_crowns)) %>% 
    # make an id
    dplyr::mutate(xxx_id = dplyr::row_number())
  
  # intersection for tp's
  i_temp <-
    pred_crowns %>% 
    dplyr::rename_with(
      .fn = ~stringr::str_replace(.x, "^xxx_", "xxx_pred_")
      , .cols = tidyselect::starts_with("xxx_")
    ) %>% 
    sf::st_intersection(
      ref_points %>% 
        dplyr::select(xxx_id,xxx_match_col) %>% 
        dplyr::rename_with(
          .fn = ~stringr::str_replace(.x, "^xxx_", "xxx_ref_")
          , .cols = tidyselect::starts_with("xxx_")
        )
    ) %>% 
    sf::st_drop_geometry() %>% 
    # absolute diff between match col
    dplyr::mutate(
      xxx_abs_diff = abs(xxx_pred_match_col - xxx_ref_match_col)
    ) %>% 
    # sorting is key to make the purrr::reduce work how we want it
    dplyr::arrange(
      desc(xxx_pred_match_col)
      , xxx_pred_id
      , xxx_abs_diff
    )
  # i_temp %>% dplyr::glimpse()
  
  # if there even are any matches
  if(nrow(i_temp)>1){
    # ?purrr::reduce
    # purrr::reduce(letters[1:5], paste, sep = ".")
    # 1:3  %>% reduce(`+`)
    match_temp <- purrr::reduce(
      # go through all rows except first since we start there
      .x = c(2:nrow(i_temp))
      # start with the first row
      , .init = i_temp %>% dplyr::slice(1) # = iter_temp
      , .f = function(iter_temp, i){
        
        #ids of curr row
        pred_id  <- i_temp$xxx_pred_id[i]
        ref_id <- i_temp$xxx_ref_id[i]
        
        # either one used?
        pred_used  <- pred_id %in% iter_temp$xxx_pred_id
        ref_used <- ref_id %in% iter_temp$xxx_ref_id
        
        # add if freee
        if(!pred_used && !ref_used) {
          return(
            iter_temp %>% 
              dplyr::bind_rows(
                dplyr::slice(i_temp, i)
              )
          )
        }else{
          # return current state
          return(iter_temp)
        }
    })
    # match_temp %>% dplyr::glimpse()
    # match_temp %>% dplyr::count(xxx_pred_id) %>% dplyr::filter(n>1) %>% nrow()
    # match_temp %>% dplyr::count(xxx_ref_id) %>% dplyr::filter(n>1) %>% nrow()
  }else{
    match_temp <- i_temp
  }
  # match_temp %>% dplyr::glimpse()
  # these are matches
  return_df <- match_temp %>% 
    dplyr::rename(
      ref_match_idx = xxx_ref_id
      , pred_match_idx = xxx_pred_id
    ) %>% 
    dplyr::select(dplyr::all_of(c(
      "ref_match_idx"
      , "pred_match_idx"
    ))) %>% 
    dplyr::mutate(match_grp = "true positive")
  # return_df %>% dplyr::glimpse()

  return_df <-
    return_df %>% 
    # if reference but no predictions...they are all omissions (FN)
    dplyr::bind_rows(
      ref_points %>% 
        dplyr::filter(
          !(xxx_id %in% match_temp$xxx_ref_id)
        ) %>% 
        sf::st_drop_geometry() %>% 
        dplyr::rename(
          ref_match_idx = xxx_id
        ) %>% 
        dplyr::mutate(pred_match_idx = as.numeric(NA)) %>% 
        dplyr::select(dplyr::all_of(c(
          "ref_match_idx"
          , "pred_match_idx"
        ))) %>% 
        dplyr::mutate(match_grp = "omission")  
    ) %>% 
    # if predictions but no reference...they are all commissions (FP)
    dplyr::bind_rows(
      pred_crowns %>% 
        dplyr::filter(
          !(xxx_id %in% match_temp$xxx_pred_id)
        ) %>% 
        sf::st_drop_geometry() %>% 
        dplyr::rename(
          pred_match_idx = xxx_id
        ) %>% 
        dplyr::mutate(ref_match_idx = as.numeric(NA)) %>% 
        dplyr::select(dplyr::all_of(c(
          "ref_match_idx"
          , "pred_match_idx"
        ))) %>% 
        dplyr::mutate(match_grp = "commission")
    ) %>% 
    # add on treeID
    dplyr::left_join(
      ref_points %>% 
        sf::st_drop_geometry() %>%
        dplyr::select(xxx_id, treeID) %>% 
        dplyr::rename(
          ref_match_idx = xxx_id
          , ref_treeID = treeID
        )
      , by = "ref_match_idx"
    ) %>% 
    # add on treeID
    dplyr::left_join(
      pred_crowns %>% 
        sf::st_drop_geometry() %>% 
        dplyr::select(xxx_id, treeID) %>% 
        dplyr::rename(
          pred_match_idx = xxx_id
          , pred_treeID = treeID
        )
      , by = "pred_match_idx"
    )
    
  # return_df %>% dplyr::glimpse()
  # return_df %>% View()
  # return_df %>% dplyr::count(match_grp)
  
  # make match_grp factor
    return_df <- return_df %>% 
      dplyr::mutate(
        match_grp = factor(
          match_grp
          , ordered = T
          , levels = c(
            "true positive"
            , "commission"
            , "omission"
          )
        ) %>% forcats::fct_rev()
      )
    return(return_df)
}
```

remember, we have predictions for many different window functions for each plot. we need a function to iterate over each set of predictions (i.e. window function) for a single plot. this is where we'll filter the predictions to attempt to match the field data collection protocol (e.g. measure trees >= 10 cm DBH)

```{r}
ws_iter_instance_match_fn <- function(
  plot_sf # needs plot_id # should be a single plot
  , ref_pts # needs plot_id
  , pred_polys # needs plot_id
  # minimum tree height
  , min_ht_m = NA
  # -OR- minimum DBH
  , min_dbh_cm = NA
){
  if(
    !any( stringr::str_equal(names(plot_sf),"plot_id") )
  ){
    stop("`plot_sf` needs column named `plot_id`")
  }
  if(
    !any( stringr::str_equal(names(ref_pts),"plot_id") )
  ){
    stop("`ref_pts` needs column named `plot_id`")
  }
  if(
    !any( stringr::str_equal(names(pred_polys),"plot_id") )
  ){
    stop("`pred_polys` needs column named `plot_id`")
  }
  
  # pred polys
  pred_polys <- 
    pred_polys %>% 
    dplyr::filter(
      plot_id == plot_sf$plot_id[1]
    )
  
  # reference points
  ref_pts <- 
    ref_pts %>% 
    dplyr::filter(
      plot_id == plot_sf$plot_id[1]
    )
  
  # filter based on field survey limit
  if(
    !is.na(as.numeric(min_dbh_cm))
  ){
    # do they exist? .... PRED
    if(
      any( stringr::str_equal(names(pred_polys),"fia_est_dbh_cm_upper") )
    ){
      pred_polys <- pred_polys %>% 
        dplyr::filter(
          dplyr::coalesce(fia_est_dbh_cm_upper,0) >= as.numeric(min_dbh_cm)
        )
    }else if(
      any( stringr::str_equal(names(pred_polys),"dbh_cm") )
    ){
      pred_polys <- pred_polys %>% 
        dplyr::filter(
          dplyr::coalesce(dbh_cm,0) >= as.numeric(min_dbh_cm)
        )
    }else{
      stop("`pred_polys` needs column named `dbh_cm`")
    }
    
    # do they exist? .... REF
    if(
      any( stringr::str_equal(names(ref_pts),"dbh_cm") )
    ){
      ref_pts <- ref_pts %>% 
        dplyr::filter(
          dplyr::coalesce(dbh_cm,0) >= as.numeric(min_dbh_cm)
        )
    }else{
      stop("`ref_pts` needs column named `dbh_cm`")
    }
  }else if(
    !is.na(as.numeric(min_ht_m))
  ){
    # do they exist? .... PRED
    if(
      any( stringr::str_equal(names(pred_polys),"tree_height_m") )
    ){
      pred_polys <- pred_polys %>% 
        dplyr::filter(
          dplyr::coalesce(tree_height_m,0) >= as.numeric(min_ht_m)
        )
    }else{
      stop("`pred_polys` needs column named `tree_height_m`")
    }
    
    # do they exist? .... REF
    if(
      any( stringr::str_equal(names(ref_pts),"tree_height_m") )
    ){
      ref_pts <- ref_pts %>% 
        dplyr::filter(
          dplyr::coalesce(tree_height_m,0) >= as.numeric(min_ht_m)
        )
    }else{
      stop("`ref_pts` needs column named `tree_height_m`")
    }
  }
  
  if(nrow(ref_pts)==0){return(NULL)}
  
  # map over it
  if(
    !any( stringr::str_equal(names(pred_polys),"ws_fn_nm") )
  ){
    stop("`pred_polys` needs column named `ws_fn_nm` ... see ws_testtest_fn() ")
  }
  if(
    !any( stringr::str_equal(names(pred_polys),"tree_x") )
  ){
    stop("`pred_polys` needs column named `tree_x` ... see ws_testtest_fn() ")
  }
  if(
    !any( stringr::str_equal(names(pred_polys),"tree_y") )
  ){
    stop("`pred_polys` needs column named `tree_y` ... see ws_testtest_fn() ")
  }
  
  # map it
  instance_match_ans <- 
    unique(pred_polys$ws_fn_nm) %>% 
    purrr::set_names() %>%
    purrr::map(function(nm){
      # which preds?
      these_pred_polys <- 
        pred_polys %>% 
        dplyr::filter(
          ws_fn_nm == nm
        )
      # instance match
      ###########################################################################################
      ## this is for matching predicted crowns to reference points
      ###########################################################################################
      im <-
        instance_match_fn(
          pred_crowns = these_pred_polys
          , ref_points = ref_pts
        )
      # ###########################################################################################
      # ## this is for matching predicted points to reference points
      # ###########################################################################################
      # im <- 
      #   reference_prediction_match(
      #     pred_data = these_pred_polys
      #     , ref_data = ref_pts
      #     , max_dist_m = 2
      #     , max_error_pct = 0.5
      #   ) %>% 
      #   ground_truth_prediction_match()
      # remove commission points outside plot boundary?
      # remove commission points outside plot boundary?
      # get rid of commissions outside of plot
      outs <- 
        these_pred_polys %>% 
        dplyr::mutate(
          pred_match_idx = dplyr::row_number()
        ) %>% 
        sf::st_drop_geometry() %>%
        sf::st_as_sf(coords = c("tree_x", "tree_y"), crs = sf::st_crs(pred_polys)) %>% 
        sf::st_filter(
          plot_sf %>% sf::st_union() %>% sf::st_transform(sf::st_crs(pred_polys))
          , .predicate = sf::st_disjoint
        ) %>% 
        sf::st_drop_geometry() %>% 
        dplyr::select(pred_match_idx) %>% 
        dplyr::mutate(is_out = T)
      
      return_df <- 
        im %>% 
        dplyr::left_join(
          outs
          , by = "pred_match_idx"
        ) %>% 
        dplyr::filter(
          !(match_grp == "commission" & dplyr::coalesce(is_out,F)==T)
        ) %>% 
        dplyr::select(-is_out)
      return(return_df)
    }) %>% 
    purrr::list_rbind(names_to = "ws_fn_nm")
  
  
  return(instance_match_ans)
}
```

now, we need to iterate over all plots at a study site

```{r}
plot_iter_instance_match_fn <- function(
  ref_plots
  , ref_pts
  # needs plot_id
  , pred_polys
  # minimum tree height
  , min_ht_m = NA
  # -OR- minimum DBH
  , min_dbh_cm = NA
) {
  if(
    !any( stringr::str_equal(names(ref_plots),"plot_id") )
  ){
    stop("`ref_plots` needs column named `plot_id`")
  }
  if(
    !any( stringr::str_equal(names(ref_pts),"plot_id") )
  ){
    stop("`ref_pts` needs column named `plot_id`")
  }
  if(
    !any( stringr::str_equal(names(pred_polys),"plot_id") )
  ){
    stop("`pred_polys` needs column named `plot_id`")
  }
  
  ws_iter_instance_match_ans <- 
    unique(ref_plots$plot_id) %>% 
    purrr::set_names() %>% 
    purrr::map(
      \(pid)
      ws_iter_instance_match_fn(
        # needs plot_id # should be a single plot
        plot_sf = ref_plots %>% dplyr::filter(plot_id==pid) 
        # needs plot_id
        , ref_pts = ref_pts 
        # needs plot_id
        , pred_polys = pred_polys
        # minimum tree height
        , min_ht_m = min_ht_m
        # -OR- minimum DBH
        , min_dbh_cm = min_dbh_cm
      )
  ) %>% 
  purrr::list_rbind(names_to = "plot_id")
  
  return(ws_iter_instance_match_ans)
}
```

lastly, we need a function to aggregate these instance segmentation counts (TP, FP, and FN) to evaluate the overall accuracy of the tree segmentation method. then, we'll select the best window function and apply that across the entire study area.

```{r}
###############################################################
###############################################################
###############################################################
###############################################################
# first function takes df with cols tp_n, fp_n, and fn_n to calculate rates
###############################################################
###############################################################
###############################################################
###############################################################
confusion_matrix_scores_fn <- function(df){
  df %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(
    omission_rate = dplyr::case_when(
      dplyr::coalesce(tp_n,0) == 0 & dplyr::coalesce(fn_n,0) == 0 ~ 0 # if there are no actual trees, there is nothing to miss
      , dplyr::coalesce(tp_n,0) == 0 & dplyr::coalesce(fn_n,0) > 0 ~ 1 # every single actual tree was missed
      , dplyr::coalesce(fn_n,0) == 0 & dplyr::coalesce(tp_n,0) > 0 ~ 0
      , T ~ fn_n/(tp_n+fn_n)
    ) # False Negative Rate or Miss Rate
    , commission_rate = dplyr::case_when(
      dplyr::coalesce(tp_n,0) == 0 & dplyr::coalesce(fp_n,0) == 0 ~ 0 # if no predictions are made, the model could not have made any commission errors
      , dplyr::coalesce(fp_n,0) == 0 & dplyr::coalesce(tp_n,0) > 0 ~ 0
      , T ~ fp_n/(tp_n+fp_n)
    ) # False Positive Rate
    , precision = dplyr::case_when(
      dplyr::coalesce(tp_n,0) == 0 & dplyr::coalesce(fp_n,0) == 0 ~ 1 # if no predictions are made, the model made zero incorrect positive claims
      , dplyr::coalesce(tp_n,0) == 0 & dplyr::coalesce(fp_n,0) > 0 ~ 0
      , T ~ tp_n/(tp_n+fp_n)
    )
    , recall = dplyr::case_when(
      dplyr::coalesce(tp_n,0) == 0 & dplyr::coalesce(fn_n,0) == 0 ~ 1 # if there are no actual trees, there is nothing to miss
      , dplyr::coalesce(tp_n,0) == 0 & dplyr::coalesce(fn_n,0) > 0 ~ 0 # every single actual tree was missed
      , T ~ tp_n/(tp_n+fn_n)
    )
    , f_score = dplyr::case_when(
      dplyr::coalesce(precision,0) == 0 | dplyr::coalesce(recall,0) == 0 ~ 0
      , T ~ 2 * ( (precision*recall)/(precision+recall) )
    )    
  ) 
}
###############################################################
###############################################################
###############################################################
###############################################################
# aggregate results from ground_truth_prediction_match()
###############################################################
###############################################################
###############################################################
###############################################################
agg_ground_truth_match <- function(ground_truth_prediction_match_ans) {
  if(nrow(ground_truth_prediction_match_ans)==0){return(NULL)}
  if( !(names(ground_truth_prediction_match_ans) %>% stringr::str_equal("match_grp") %>% any()) ){stop("ground_truth_prediction_match_ans must contain `match_grp` column")}
  
  # check for difference columns (contains "_diff") and calc rmse for only those to return a single line df with colums for each diff_rmse
    if(
      (ground_truth_prediction_match_ans %>% 
        sf::st_drop_geometry() %>% 
        dplyr::select(tidyselect::starts_with("diff_") | tidyselect::starts_with("pct_diff_")) %>% 
        ncol() )>0
    ){
      # get rmse and mean difference/error for all columns with "_diff" but not "pct_diff"
      # get mape for all columns with "pct_diff" but not "diff_"
      rmse_df <- 
        ground_truth_prediction_match_ans %>% 
        sf::st_drop_geometry() %>% 
        dplyr::ungroup() %>% 
        dplyr::select(
          tidyselect::starts_with("diff_")
          | tidyselect::starts_with("pct_diff_")
        ) %>%
        tidyr::pivot_longer(dplyr::everything(), values_drop_na = T) %>% 
        dplyr::group_by(name) %>% 
        dplyr::summarise(
          sq = sum(value^2, na.rm = T)
          , mean = mean(value, na.rm = T)
          , sumabs = sum(abs(value), na.rm = T)
          , nomiss = sum(!is.na(value))
        ) %>% 
        dplyr::ungroup() %>% 
        dplyr::mutate(
          rmse = dplyr::case_when(
            dplyr::coalesce(nomiss,0)==0 ~ as.numeric(NA)
            , T ~ sqrt(sq/nomiss)
          )
          , mape = dplyr::case_when(
            dplyr::coalesce(nomiss,0)==0 ~ as.numeric(NA)
            , T ~ sumabs/nomiss
          )
        ) %>% 
        # NA nonsense values
        dplyr::mutate(
          mape = dplyr::case_when(
            stringr::str_starts(name, "pct_diff_") ~ mape
            , T ~ as.numeric(NA)
          )
          , rmse = dplyr::case_when(
            stringr::str_starts(name, "pct_diff_") ~ as.numeric(NA)
            , T ~ rmse
          )
          , mean = dplyr::case_when(
            stringr::str_starts(name, "pct_diff_") ~ as.numeric(NA)
            , T ~ mean
          )
        ) %>% 
        dplyr::select(name,rmse,mean,mape) %>% 
        tidyr::pivot_wider(
          names_from = name
          , values_from = c(rmse,mean,mape)
          , names_glue = "{name}_{.value}"
        ) %>% 
        # remove columns with NA in all rows
        dplyr::select( dplyr::where( ~!all(is.na(.x)) ) )
      
      if(
        dplyr::coalesce(nrow(rmse_df),0)==0
        || dplyr::coalesce(ncol(rmse_df),0)==0
      ){
        # empty df
        rmse_df <- dplyr::tibble()
      }
    }else{
      # empty df
      rmse_df <- dplyr::tibble()
    }
  
  # count by match group
    agg <-
      ground_truth_prediction_match_ans %>% 
      sf::st_drop_geometry() %>% 
      dplyr::ungroup() %>% 
      dplyr::count(match_grp) %>% 
      dplyr::mutate(
        match_grp = dplyr::recode_values(
          match_grp
          , "true positive"~"tp"
          , "commission"~"fp"
          , "omission"~"fn"
        )
      )
    # true positive, false positive, false negative rates
    return_df <- dplyr::tibble(match_grp = c("tp","fp","fn")) %>% 
      dplyr::left_join(agg, by = "match_grp") %>% 
      dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(.cols = c(n), .fn = ~dplyr::coalesce(.x,0))) %>% 
      tidyr::pivot_wider(
        names_from = match_grp
        , values_from = c(n)
        , names_glue = "{match_grp}_{.value}"
      )
    # rates, precision, recall, f-score
    return_df <- confusion_matrix_scores_fn(return_df)
    # add rmse
    if(nrow(rmse_df)>0){
      return_df <- return_df %>% dplyr::bind_cols(rmse_df)
    }
  # return
  return(return_df)
}
```

we can process more of the CHM data using only this selected window function within `cloud2trees::raster2trees()` and we'll also estimate DBH (`cloud2trees::trees_dbh()`) and relative tree height. For relative tree height, I have defined a custom function using a highly efficient data processing routine with `RANN::nn2()` which kd-tree to find the p number of near neighbours for each point in an input/output dataset; the advantage of the kd-tree is that it runs in O(M log M) time. This custom function is for eventual integration into `cloud2trees::trees_competition()`.

```{r}
# ?RANN::nn2
# ?cloud2trees::trees_competition
competition_radius_m <- sqrt((30*30*2*2)/pi)
get_relative_height_fn <- function(df, radius) {
    # Use the X and Y coordinates of the reference to build the tree.
    coords_temp <- 
      df %>% 
      sf::st_drop_geometry() %>% 
      sf::st_as_sf(coords = c("tree_x", "tree_y"), crs = sf::st_crs(df), remove = F) %>% 
      dplyr::mutate(
        X = sf::st_coordinates(.)[,1] %>% as.numeric()
        , Y = sf::st_coordinates(.)[,2] %>% as.numeric()
      ) %>% 
      dplyr::select(X,Y) %>% 
      sf::st_drop_geometry()
    # coords_temp %>% dplyr::glimpse()
    
    # perform a fixed-radius search using RANN::nn2
    # ?RANN::nn2
    nn_ans_temp <- RANN::nn2(
      # the point cloud xy data (builds the kd-tree on this)
      data = coords_temp
      # the seed point xy data (number of columns must be the same as data)
      , query = coords_temp
      # maximum number of neighbors to find per query
      , k = nrow(coords_temp)
      # the search radius (rcyl)
      , radius = radius
      , searchtype = "radius"
    )
    # nn_ans_temp %>% dplyr::glimpse()
    # nn_ans_temp$nn.idx[1:19,2:22]
    
    # iterate through the results to compute metrics
    w_ht <- 
      1:nrow(df) %>% 
      purrr::map(
        function(i) {
          # which seed?
          which_seed <- df %>% dplyr::slice(i)
          
          # get indices of points in the current radius (0 means no point found)
          # rad_pts <- nn_ans_temp$nn.idx[i, 2:ncol(nn_ans_temp$nn.idx)] # filter out self-idx in col 1
          rad_pts <- nn_ans_temp$nn.idx[i, ] # DON'T filter out self-idx in col 1
          rad_pts <- rad_pts[rad_pts > 0] 
          
          # if no other points, it's the tallest
          if (dplyr::coalesce(length(rad_pts),0) < 2) {
            return(
              which_seed %>% dplyr::mutate(rel_tree_height_m = 1)
            )
          }
          
          # get ht values using the indices
          ht_values <- df$tree_height_m[rad_pts]
          
          # relative ht
          my_rel_ht <- which_seed$tree_height_m / max(ht_values,na.rm=T)
          return(
            which_seed %>% dplyr::mutate(rel_tree_height_m = my_rel_ht)
          )
        }
      ) %>% 
      dplyr::bind_rows()
    
    return(w_ht)
}

#     # .... but we'll go a little smaller because we're confident in the ITD trees and heights
```
